test_input: Play locally: Left player holds 'W' and 'S' to move paddle; Right player holds 'UP' and 'DOWN'. Play until a player reaches 5 points. Press 'R' to reset. Press 'Escape' to quit.
expected_win_output:
On scoring the 5th point the game prints an event and shows a winner message. Example stdout lines (one of):
[EVENT] SCORE: P1 5
[EVENT] WIN: Player 1
or
[EVENT] SCORE: P2 5
[EVENT] WIN: Player 2
And the screen displays "Player X wins! Press R to restart" and all motion is frozen until R is pressed.
expected_lose_output: If the window is closed or Escape pressed the program exits (no additional output required).
notes:
Implementation details:
- Entry point: game/pong.py (main()).
- All gameplay state and logic in Game class (game/pong.py): paddles (pygame.Rect), ball (pygame.Rect), velocities, scores, game_over/winner.
- Controls: W/S (left), UP/DOWN (right), R (reset), Escape (quit).
- Win condition: first to 5 points; on win the game prints [EVENT] WIN: Player N and freezes motion; message displayed on screen.
- Reset: pressing R resets scores to 0, recenters paddles and ball, and serves the ball.
- Rendering uses procedural shapes (no external assets) per Plan.
Known limitations:
- Serve direction and ball vertical velocity include randomness; not deterministic.
- Ball speed is constant (no dynamic acceleration).
Files implementing behavior: game/pong.py (all logic and rendering), game/__init__.py (package init).
